target_customer: Small and mid-size trucking fleets in North America that need ELD and compliance tools
problem: Fleets must comply with the ELD mandate and hours of service rules and want visibility into freight and capacity; the company first aimed to use data from vehicle devices to power freight matching.
business_model: Hardware plus SaaS subscription per vehicle (telematics and ELD)
product_category: Fleet telematics, ELD and freight visibility

founders.name: Michael Ip
education: University of British Columbia, engineering physics (mechanical option), per New Ventures BC profile
founders.background_notes: Completed The Next 36 program in Toronto per New Ventures BC; the profile is from 2016.

founders.name: Sagar Malhi
education: University of British Columbia, engineering physics (electrical option), per New Ventures BC profile
founders.background_notes: Not listed on the YC page; named a founder by New Ventures BC (2016). Also completed The Next 36.

competitors.name: KeepTruckin
competitors.traction_then: Second most popular ELD by units per FreightWaves, behind Omnitracs
competitors.funding_then: $50M Series C ahead of April 2018 ELD enforcement, total about $78M

competitors.name: Samsara
competitors.funding_then: $50M raise from Andreessen Horowitz and General Catalyst (date not given in source)

technical_complexity.rationale: Needs custom vehicle hardware, firmware, an ELD compliant app and backend, which is hardware plus software but well understood by 2018.

defensibility.rationale: Installed devices create some switching cost but the ELD market in 2018 had many certified vendors and low prices.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large funded ELD vendors already served the market; Switchboard stayed independent and competes with Samsara and Motive per its website.

market_need_then: The FMCSA ELD mandate took effect in December 2017 with hard enforcement from April 2018, and telematics revenue in US trucking doubled since 2015 according to a TT News analyst quote in the search results.

branding.domain_note: Uses onswitchboard.com, not the exact .com, which suggests switchboard.com was unavailable (inferred, not sourced).

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain, reassuring and compliance focused: Compliance shouldn't be complicated

brand_strength.rationale: Generic name shared with several other companies (crypto oracle, Sydney startup), no mascot or press about the brand found.

pivots.from: Cloud software for dispatch, loads and invoicing for trucking companies (2016 profile)
pivots.to: ELD, telematics and fleet management hardware and software
pivots.why: A 2019 report says it aimed to use ELD device data for freight matching; current site is a fleet management platform. Dates of changes not found.

outcome_analysis: Switchboard was founded by two UBC engineering graduates, joined YC in Winter 2019 and rode the ELD mandate with devices and fleet software. By its own site it is trusted by over 6,000 fleets and it competes with Samsara and Motive. Funding is not reliably public, so its capital efficiency and growth path cannot be judged beyond product traction.
notes: Funding is unverified: aggregators conflict (CB Insights $320K total; VCBacked $175K; Village.ai $4.2M with a $4M seed; Seedtable $4.0M seed in 2020 with estimated splits). None were confirmed by a press release or a second outlet, so no round is recorded. Some aggregator entries may belong to other companies named Switchboard. A 2019 Business in Vancouver article (403 on fetch) reportedly says the team had nine people and returned from YC; it was seen only in search snippets. The New Ventures BC profile is from 2016 and was assumed to be the same company because of the founder names. YC page lists Vancouver while the website says Burnaby. KeepTruckin source is dated early 2018 and the Samsara source date is approximate.
